node.title: A primitive LS6 base gives a complete determinant coordinate chart
node.statement: Fix one primitive candidate (D_0,Q_0,V_0) in a guarded LS6 atom and put h=ell-2a. The map from the complete monic unguarded LS6 slice to K[X]_{<=h}, D mapsto H=D_0Q-DQ_0, is an affine bijection. Its inverse is explicit: R_H=rem_{D_0}(-H Q_0^{-1}), D_H=D_0+R_H, Q_H=(H+D_HQ_0)/D_0, and V_H=(D_HV_0-MH)/D_0. For coordinates H,G, the pair determinant is (D_HG-D_GH)/D_0 and again has degree at most h. Thus all formal multi-determinant and Plucker identities already hold on the whole ambient slice and cannot by themselves reduce its maximum. Guarded split points are exactly the coordinates for which D_H divides the core locator and the printed root-local primitive inequalities hold. The remaining theorem is therefore a split-root/owner census in this chart, not abstract determinant compatibility.
